presentation_summary: Known Behcet disease with recurrent oral ulcers and panuveitis, previously treated with azathioprine and cyclosporine.
Two weeks of fever and sore throat, then higher fever to 39 C.
Three days of photophobia, right body weakness, difficulty walking, and acute loss of consciousness.
Neurologic exam showed GCS 8/15, vertical nystagmus, right foot myoclonus, brisk reflexes, and bilateral Babinski signs.

MRI showed bilateral asymmetric signal abnormalities involving corpus callosum, internal capsules, left thalamus, meso-diencephalic junction, midbrain, and hippocampi with edema and leptomeningeal enhancement.

risk_context.source_text_value: received azathioprine and cyclosporine for 5 years for Behcet disease
